<document id=DOC_excerpt_settle_order>
DISCOUNT_BY_TIER = {"standard": 20, "premium": 30}

def settle_order(account_tier, total_amount, coupon_codes, coupon_lookup):
    discount = DISCOUNT_BY_TIER[account_tier]
    coupon_sum = coupon_lookup[coupon_codes[0]]
    amount_owed = total_amount * discount / 100 - coupon_sum
    return amount_owed
</document>

The module below redeems coupon codes by looking them up. Nothing in
it limits how long a code stays redeemable, so every code ever issued
remains valid indefinitely.

Recommend how the design should bound a code's lifetime, and say what
the lookup would have to carry for that bound to be enforceable.

response.text:
Give every code an absolute expiry and refuse redemption when that instant has passed. Issuance-time policy alone cannot enforce this, because the redeem path never rechecks age.

The lookup must stop returning a bare amount. Each entry needs at least:

- the coupon value
- `expires_at` (an absolute timestamp, not a duration)

Optionally also `valid_from`, if codes should not redeem before a start time.

`settle_order` (or the lookup wrapper it calls) must read `expires_at`, compare it to the current time, and reject the code before applying the value. A TTL stored only at issue time is not enough: without `expires_at` (or an equivalent issued-at plus TTL carried in the lookup and checked at redeem), every previously issued code stays valid forever.
